subject: Evidence handling & post-incident log hold for Acme - next steps
messages:
From: Laura Briggs <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Chen <forensics@thirdparty.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Request: preserve logs + scope for Acme incident

Hi Mina,

We identified unusual outgoing connections from an internal service (app-prod-2) at ~04:30 UTC this morning. Our team is starting an internal review and we need Redwood to place an immediate legal/forensic hold on any logs, telemetry, and KV cache snapshots related to the Acme tenant for the time window 2027-02-14 04:00–05:00 UTC.

Specifically we need:
- Preservation of application and request logs, LB logs, and any inference runtime traces for the window above
- A hash-signed manifest of collected files and collection timestamps
- Confirmation of the region(s) where collected artifacts will be stored and the retention schedule

Can you confirm you’ve placed a hold and share your proposed retention timeline and mechanics for secure handoff? We will engage our forensics vendor (Adam CC’d) for collection verification.

Thanks,
Laura Briggs
Head of Security — Acme Corporation
security@acme-corp.com

Attachment: none

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Briggs <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Adam Chen <forensics@thirdparty.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: preserve logs + scope for Acme incident

Laura — thanks for the heads up and sorry you’re dealing with this. I’ve placed an immediate administrative hold on all Acme tenant artifacts and notified infra/forensics internally. High-level plan below; I’ll follow up with precise manifests within the hour.

Immediate actions (already kicked off):
- Admin hold applied across retention policies for Acme tenant (no automatic deletion)
- Snapshotting request logs, runtime traces, and endpoint access logs for 2027-02-14 03:45–05:15 UTC to give some context window
- Marking KV cache snapshots read-only and exporting last-applied keys where possible

Retention proposal for now: 90 days in encrypted archive with audit log of access and deletion actions. We can extend if Acme requests longer for legal reasons. If you need shorter/longer, tell me the target and we’ll adjust.

Storage and access: collected artifacts will be encrypted at rest with a customer-scoped CMK and stored in US-East (us-east-1). Collection will be staged under a locked bucket s3://redwood-incident-archive/acme/20270215 and will only be accessible to the incident response group and to the Acme-designated forensics contacts.

I’ve attached a short checklist for our collection team (initial-collection-instructions.txt) and our standard forensics checklist (forensics-checklist.xlsx). Adam — if you want to join the live handoff call we’ll set up a meeting for verification.

Next steps I’ll take:
- Send internal collection task and expected timestamp manifest
- Share proof-of-possession hashes once artifacts are uploaded
- Provide deletion timeline and deletion proof when the matter closes

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Security Partnerships — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Attachment: initial-collection-instructions.txt, forensics-checklist.xlsx

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Laura Briggs <security@acme-corp.com>, Adam Chen <forensics@thirdparty.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: preserve logs + scope for Acme incident — collection request

Team — forwarding Acme’s request. Please treat as an urgent incident hold. Requirements:
- Capture request and runtime traces for tenant "acme-corp" covering 2027-02-14 03:45–05:15 UTC; include 15 minutes padding on both sides.
- Export KV cache snapshot for inference nodes that served acme-corp during that window (include last-applied seq ids).
- Produce a timestamped manifest (UTC) with SHA256 hashes for each artifact.
- Store artifacts to: s3://redwood-incident-archive/acme/20270215 and set bucket/object ACL to IR-only (no auto-delete).
- Note residency requirement: store in us-east-1; use CMK rwf-acme-key.

Please confirm estimated collection completion and provide the manifest when ready. If you need additional compute snapshots or GPU process dumps, call it out — we can authorize.

Forwarded message below (original from Laura).

—Mina

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Briggs <security@acme-corp.com>, Adam Chen <forensics@thirdparty.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 15:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evidence handling & post-incident log hold for Acme - next steps

Laura / Adam — quick update and formal confirmation of the post-incident handling plan:

1) What we preserved
- Full export of request logs, LB logs, runtime traces, and KV cache snapshots for 2027-02-14 03:45–05:15 UTC (stored as objects in the S3 paths Vivek listed).
- Collection manifest with SHA256 hashes (attached by Vivek).

2) Residency and encryption
- Stored only in us-east-1.
- Encrypted with customer-scoped CMK (arn above). Access is limited to incident response roles and Acme-designated vendor principals.

3) Retention & deletion timeline
- Default retention: 90 days from collection (so scheduled deletion 2027-05-16).
- If Acme requests extension for legal/forensic reasons, we will place an extended hold and provide a timeline for deletion.
- Deletion proof: when deletion occurs we will provide a signed proof-of-deletion package (object list + deletion timestamps + KMS detached key proof).

4) Handoff verification
- Adam, you can verify hashes either by read-only S3 role (we will provision) or we can deliver a signed tarball over a secure channel. Let us know preference.

5) Next actions
- If you want certificates of deletion or chained signatures for chain-of-custody, confirm now so we can build the package.
- I’ll update the SEC-IR ticket (SEC-3421) and attach the handoff playbook (log-handoff-playbook.pdf). Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-3421

Thanks — we’ll keep the hold in place until you tell us otherwise.

—Mina
Director, Security Partnerships — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

Attachments: log-handoff-playbook.pdf
